findings.message: A different agent (Claude) checked the work in a separate headless process.

These are planning artifacts: a @wip feature, the ticket, the dimensions draft and an implementation ledger with every row unchecked. The ledger has the same 17 scenarios as the feature (R1: 3, R2: 10, R3: 4). Its scenario names match exactly, and nothing is marked RED or GREEN. The scenarios follow the R1–R3 requirements and the CI-provenance design in the context files. That includes refusing invented execution even when a fresh review approves it, refusing arbitrary uploads, keeping candidate code away from the signer, blocking an older pass when a newer attempt failed or is unfinished, refusing an expired checkpoint, preserving history, keeping ordinary prerequisites, and not closing work automatically. Live gates in the ledger stop local Docker or mocked results from earning GREEN for the isolation and latency scenarios, and done_when separately requires live runs and walkthroughs on each installed host. I found no concrete error that would let the user-facing claim be reported as satisfied while false. The remaining issues are traceability and completeness gaps, reported as warnings.

The demo scenario 'Explicit EP9 completion preserves its actual history' is tagged for claude-code, openai-codex and cursor, but the ledger gives it only one RED/GREEN/REFACTOR row. Unlike the isolation and latency scenarios, the ledger also has no live-gate note saying that installed walkthroughs on all three hosts are needed for GREEN. done_when does list that requirement, but GREEN could be checked after one host or a synthetic adapter fixture. Either add a live-gate note or give each host its own row.

No feature scenario or named table-driven case covers a newer successful retry paired with a review bound to the older observation. The design says a retry 'can become current only with a new observation-bound review and checkpoint'. 'Changed bound proof revokes current credit' may cover this, but that is not stated. Name it as a variation under that scenario so the test is required to tell the two cases apart.

The feature's rule titles differ from spec.md. R1 says 'Only the fixed EP9 proof is eligible' where the spec says '...delivery is eligible', and R2 says 'Execution and review authority are independent and revocable' where the spec says 'Authority is independent and revocable'. The ledger uses a third set of headings ('Fixed EP9 eligibility', etc.) with no rule IDs. If any tool matches titles rather than tag IDs, traceability could break. Align the titles or add the R-IDs to the ledger headings.

In the 'Candidate execution cannot reach signing authority' scenario, the Then step ('cannot issue or replace a trusted successful execution claim') can pass trivially if the candidate's credential-read or artifact-replacement attempts never actually ran. The live proof should record evidence that each attempt (GITHUB_TOKEN, ACTIONS_RUNTIME_TOKEN, OIDC/artifact credentials, artifact replacement between execution and signing) was executed and failed. Otherwise this check does not show anything.

The 'Live closing feasibility is established before adoption' scenario is really an adoption gate, and it needs CI dispatch, which this ticket currently excludes from scope. That is consistent with the ledger's 'CI execution remains unauthorized' note. Still, it is the only scenario whose failure means going back to a design decision, not a product refusal. Consider stating that a failed measurement blocks the feature rather than becoming RED that is later fixed by relaxing the five-minute window.

The ticket's last_modified equals created even though the Work Log has later review entries. The context file spec.md also still says 'Scenarios ... have not been performed', while dimensions.md says the formal feature source now exists. Some metadata and wording is out of date. This does not block, but it should be reconciled.
